So I often post about PhysLean on my own personal social media accounts (usually LinkedIn - which is the only one I really have), but last week I created a bluesky account for news related to the project:

:link: https://bsky.app/profile/physlean.bsky.social

The idea is to post about things happening in the project, and anything else related, with the aim to increase visibility amongst physicists.

If anyone has ideas for posts or anything else related to this, or wants to help run the account, this is a thread for that :).
Twitter =)?
Made a twitter account a few days ago - although haven't put so much effort into this yet: https://x.com/PhysLean
New mastodon account: https://mathstodon.xyz/@PhysLean

fwiw i have a plan to casually blog about my first commits to physlean on my blog + some motivating statements - the substack got around 10k views a month so hopefully would give physlean some visibility. https://chillphysicsenjoyer.substack.com/
Nice! This would be very much appreciated :slight_smile: .

i am surprised to the upside about the reception of this post

#PhysLean

its got 18 substack likes, which is a lot in the substack world!
https://chillphysicsenjoyer.substack.com/p/we-should-formalise-physics
Awesome! Thanks for writing this @Afiq Hatta and helping spread the word :).
https://chillphysicsenjoyer.substack.com/p/try-to-prove-math-with-computers
a more walkthroughy post for noobs like me ;)

I am slightly concerned that people will read this post and come away with the feeling that proving 0 <= 2 in Lean is somewhat of a complicated adventure, when in fact it is just closed immediately with the mathlib tactic norm_num, something which is never mentioned in that post.

Put another way, someone reading that post might think "wow, so presumably proving 1 <= 5 is basically impossible in Lean because it was so much work to prove 0 <= 2". Might I suggest that you mention at the end that 

import Mathlib.Tactic

example : 37 ≤ 1000000 := by
  norm_num

works fine?
good point @Kevin Buzzard - it was meant to be a pretty contrived example. I think what I'll do is put a healthy disclaimer in the beginning that there are standard libraries out there!
really grateful for the feedback. i'll also put that piece of code at the bottom
@Kevin Buzzard updated the post

Would it be a good idea to have a LinkedIn page for PhysLib? Earlier i could just tag Joseph but now that there are more maintainers and even more repos contributing to the project, I think it's better to have an independent linkedin page just like there's one for twitter to reflect the more formal nature of the project?? (MathLib doesn't have a LinkedIn page interestingly)
I personally don't really know how LinkedIn pages work in this respect. Can anyone make one?

The process seems simple on linkedin.com/company/setup/new as explained by Claude. But I'm not sure of the right way it's handled by open-source projects. Here's the linkedin page for famous Kubernetes open-source project: https://www.linkedin.com/company/kubernetes/

Nice! If others think this is a good idea, I would be up for it. Though with the caveat, that the amount of time I personally have available to post on these social media accounts is massively reduced :(.
@Shlok Vaibhav done here: https://www.linkedin.com/company/physlib/. Maybe there is an easy way to add people so they can post/edit it aswell.

I ended up finding a way you can add people to the Linkedin and give them permission to post as the organization. So if anyone is particularly socially adept, and wants to have a go let me know.

Historically I use to post "weekly" summaries of things that have happened in physlib, it wasn't a lot of work, but other things got in the way. But surely it is possible to automate something like this?

It might be interesting to use NotebookLM.
I don't know if this is possible, but maybe by sending the PRs, diffs, and comments from Zulip, it could generate a weekly news report on the changes in podcast format—complete with video and perhaps a written summary.

I don't know if it's compatible, but that's the first thing that came to mind.

Yes, I think that's a handy way to generate summaries. Here's a claude generated summary for last 7 days:
Physlib — Weekly Summary (Apr 3–10, 2026)
8 commits merged, 7 PRs closed, 4 open, ~4 active contributors.
Rename landed. Joseph merged the PhysLean → Physlib rename across the codebase (#1020). Logo update PR (#1032) still open. This completes the organizational move under leanprover-community.
Quantum mechanics (Gregory Loges). Four merged PRs systematically refactoring and golfing Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector proofs (#1019, #1023, #1026), plus new radius operator limit results (#1024). A position/momentum notation refactor (#1031) is in review.
Field theory foundations (juanjfndz). MultiIndex API for local field theory (#1021), iterated space derivatives indexed by multi-indices (#1027), and regularity/support lemmas (#1028). This is laying groundwork for variational calculus.
Infra. Lean 4.29.0 toolchain bump (#1030).
Pending. Pietro Monticone has two open PRs — regularized function properties (#1022) and LRL angular momentum commutation (#991). Joseph's variational calculus restructuring (#1018) also waiting.

Is this accurate??

The issue with LLMs generating summaries is hallucinations and misinterpreting the info. While misunderstanding can be corrected by simply reading the output, hallucinations need manual cross verification of each claim, for example if the PRs mentioned here indeed exist. For that end, researchers these days run multiple agents in parallel or have the output logs of llm screened for url fetch errors but ig that's very much an open problem.

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

I ended up finding a way you can add people to the Linkedin and give them permission to post as the organization. So if anyone is particularly socially adept, and wants to have a go let me know.

Historically I use to post "weekly" summaries of things that have happened in physlib, it wasn't a lot of work, but other things got in the way. But surely it is possible to automate something like this?

Will be also nice to automate out a way to cross post to Twitter and reddit simultaneously, problem is all three platforms require different type of presentation style so that's holding back.
As to the PhysLib linkedin page, I think that will be used just to make reposts and increase visibility?? What kind of activity do you have in mind??

For the LinkedIn page I was thinking similar to what historically I was posting on twitter here: https://x.com/PhysLean. I.e. general stuff not the more opinionated stuff that I post on my personal LinkedIn. Yeah the different styles (even character lengths) ends up being a pain to deal with.

Summary above is ok, the rename bit is a bit vague, as it was rename of a directory not the whole repo which was renamed a while back, but that is context I think it would be hard for the LLM to get. What it probably can't get an idea on is the grand scheme of things.
Also never really thought about posting on reddit (except once or twice right near the start). Not entirely sure how that would work long-term.
